meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это ты у жены под каблуком!
examples.trans: You are the one under your wife's thumb!

examples.text: Ты уже должен быть дома, Сеня!
examples.trans: You should already be home, Senya!

examples.text: Ты уже пил пиво в этом месяце!
examples.trans: You already drank beer this month!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You know, I am thinking seriously here.
Lyova, do you need some help here?

examples.text: Лёва, что же ты тут натворил?
examples.trans: Lyova, what on earth have you done here?

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you need a special invitation, Maxim?

examples.text: Тогда нам тем более нужно выпить!
examples.trans: Then we have all the more reason to drink!
Let's go, Maxim, we need a drink.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.trans: Lyova, do you need some help here?
Thank you for your help, Lyova.
Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'стоять'.

examples.trans: Wait, don't go!
I'll stand here for a bit.
Vikulya, wait!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И она сразу сказала мне да!
examples.trans: And she immediately said yes to me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я могу с этим сделать?
examples.trans: And what can I do about it?

examples.text: И что ты мне тогда сделаешь?
examples.trans: And what will you do to me then?

examples.text: Что бы ты тогда один делал?
examples.trans: What would you have done alone then?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Has the Chef not arrived yet today?

examples.text: Я вчера пошёл к Елене Павловне.
examples.trans: Yesterday I went to see Elena Pavlovna.

meanings.en: to beat, to hit, to strike
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to beat, to hit', paired with 'побить'.

examples.text: Почему меня все бьют в этом доме?
examples.trans: Why does everyone beat me in this house?
The clock is striking twelve.

examples.text: Тише, Ваня, осторожно! Зачем ты бьёшь дерево ногой?
examples.trans: Easy, Vanya, be careful! Why are you kicking the tree with your foot?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, Fedya, I did that completely by accident.

examples.text: Прости, Костя, но здесь Гуля работает.
examples.trans: Sorry, Kostya, but Gulya works here.

examples.text: Прости меня, но это ради нас.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but this is for our sake.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He will probably arrive right now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'works', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Прости, Костя, но здесь Гуля работает.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто уважаю её как личность.
examples.trans: I simply respect her as a person.

examples.text: Мы с Федей хотели выпить пива.
examples.trans: Fedya and I wanted to drink some beer.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, лучше обсудим это в постели?

examples.text: Может быть, они просто сидели рядом?
examples.trans: Maybe they were simply sitting next to each other?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: You never know what might happen.
What happened?
Nothing will happen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, Viktor Petrovich, I agree.
Thank you, Lyova, I have to run to work.
How sweet, thank you, Lyova!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Lyova, do you need some help here?

I need your help.

examples.text: Лучше спокойно сидеть на нашей кухне.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'people' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне люди начали вдруг пропадать.
examples.trans: People have suddenly started disappearing in the kitchen.

examples.trans: My great journey began with this song.

examples.text: Можно я сначала быстро выйду в туалет?
examples.trans: May I quickly step out to the restroom first?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В комнату вдруг входит грозная Марина.
examples.trans: Formidable Marina suddenly enters the room.

examples.text: Если бы меня вдруг не стало?
examples.trans: If I were suddenly gone?

examples.text: На кухне люди начали вдруг пропадать.
examples.trans: People have suddenly started disappearing in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'падать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'disappear'.

examples.text: На кухне люди начали вдруг пропадать.
examples.trans: People have suddenly started disappearing in the kitchen.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и пропадать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and disappear on time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Ты всегда только о еде думаешь!

examples.trans: As usual, you do not last very long.
Please, do not touch me!
I think I need to take Gulya away.

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away', paired with 'забирать'.

examples.trans: I think I need to take Gulya away.
He will withdraw the statement.
I'll take the keys.

examples.trans: It is time for us to return back home.

examples.trans: And I am not even arguing with that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'back', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It is time for us to return back home.

examples.text: Когда в зале громко называешь его имя.
examples.trans: When you loudly call out their name in the hall.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты уже должен быть дома, Сеня!
examples.trans: You should already be home, Senya!

examples.text: У меня дома просто нет шансов.
examples.trans: I simply have no chance at home.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: It is time for us to return back home.
I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you, Viktor Petrovich, I agree.

examples.text: Интересно, кто на самом деле сильней?
examples.trans: I wonder who is actually stronger?
Who gives driver's licenses to these drivers?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'дитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'driver' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Who gives driver's licenses to these drivers?
You called a sober driver!
The bus driver opened the doors.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right').

examples.text: Ты правда хотел меня сейчас ударить?
examples.trans: Did you really want to hit me just now?

examples.text: Я же всегда говорю только правду.
examples.trans: I always tell only the truth.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.trans: Let's rather have a little more to drink.

examples.text: Давайте теперь за шефа дружно выпьем!
examples.trans: Let's all drink to the Chef together now!

examples.text: Давайте ещё раз дружно выпьем, друзья!
examples.trans: Let's have another drink together, friends!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, ought to').

examples.text: Ты уже должен быть дома, Сеня!
examples.trans: You should already be home, Senya!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Гуля должна остаться здесь со мной.
examples.trans: Gulya must stay here with me.
